executive_summary.company_overview: Kelvara Systems is a seed-stage deep-tech climate hardware company founded in 2023, headquartered in Wellington, New Zealand with an engineering team and pilot site in Manchester, UK. It builds modular thermal batteries using recycled aluminium-alloy phase-change material to store surplus renewable electricity as high-temperature heat, discharging it as industrial process heat or electricity for energy-intensive industries.
executive_summary.strongest_themes: Industrial decarbonisation and process heat electrification are the strongest funding themes — multiple major EU and UK programmes (IETF, EU Innovation Fund Heat Auction, EIC Accelerator, Horizon CID) are explicitly designed for exactly this technology and outcome. Long-duration energy storage (LDES) is a secondary but strong theme in the UK via Ofgem's cap-and-floor regime.
executive_summary.strongest_geographies: The UK and EU offer the richest grant landscape for Kelvara's technology. The UK provides direct access via IETF and Innovate UK programmes through the Manchester entity; the EU offers transformational scale via the Innovation Fund Heat Auction and EIC Accelerator, accessible through UK's Horizon association status. New Zealand has limited grant evidence in the shortlist.
executive_summary.key_constraints: Kelvara's New Zealand headquarters creates eligibility friction for EU programmes requiring an EU/associated-country entity as lead applicant — the UK entity mitigates this but must be confirmed as the applying entity. The company is pre-revenue at TRL 6, which is appropriate for most programmes but may be below the project-scale threshold for the Ofgem LDES regime. Hardware capital intensity means grant applications must demonstrate a credible path to commercial deployment, not just R&D.

strategic_recommendations.best_fit_strategy: Pursue IETF Phase 4 (feasibility stage first) and EIC Accelerator Deep Tech for Climate simultaneously as the highest-priority actions — both are open now, directly match Kelvara's core product, and provide the credibility and capital needed to reach commercial pilot. In parallel, prepare a consortium for the EU Innovation Fund Heat Auction next round and Horizon CID 2026, which offer transformational EU-scale funding.
strategic_recommendations.best_geographies: United Kingdom (IETF, Innovate UK Smart Grants, Ofgem LDES) and European Union / Horizon-associated (EIC Accelerator, EU Innovation Fund, Horizon Europe CL5/CID) — both accessible via the Manchester UK entity.
strategic_recommendations.strongest_pathways: 1) IETF Phase 4 feasibility grant (open now, direct match, manageable application); 2) EIC Accelerator Deep Tech for Climate 2026 (open now, transformational blended finance, multiple deadlines); 3) EU Innovation Fund Heat Auction next round (exact thematic match, large scale); 4) Horizon CID-2026-01-01 (consortium, Sept 2026 deadline).
strategic_recommendations.key_partnerships: An EU-based industrial partner (food processing, chemicals, or paper sector) would unlock both the EU Innovation Fund Heat Auction and Horizon Europe consortium calls. A UK university or research institute (e.g. a Faraday Institution member) would strengthen Innovate UK and Horizon applications. An Australian industrial partner would be needed to access ARENA funding in future.
strategic_recommendations.capability_gaps: Kelvara needs to: (1) confirm its UK entity is properly registered as an SME for Innovate UK eligibility; (2) establish or identify an EU-registered consortium partner for Horizon and Innovation Fund applications; (3) develop a bankable techno-economic model for the 5 MWh commercial pilot to support capital grant applications; (4) build a public track record (case study from the 500 kWh demonstration) to strengthen applications.
strategic_recommendations.key_risks: 1) NZ headquarters may disqualify Kelvara as lead applicant for EU programmes if the UK entity is not sufficiently established — verify UK entity status urgently. 2) IETF capital grants require significant co-funding (typically 30–50%) which may be challenging at seed stage. 3) EIC Accelerator has a ~5% acceptance rate and requires a compelling commercialisation narrative. 4) Hardware TRL 6 may be perceived as insufficiently de-risked for large capital grants without stronger pilot data.

opportunities.name: EU Innovation Fund — Industrial Process Heat Decarbonisation Auction (IF25 Heat Auction / next round)
opportunities.geography: EU Member States and associated countries
opportunities.max_funding: €400M+ per round (project-level amounts vary; first round awarded ~€400M across 65 projects)
opportunities.thematic_fit_explanation: The Innovation Fund Heat Auction's sole purpose is decarbonising industrial process heat — an exact match for Kelvara's core product of replacing fossil-fuel process heat with stored renewable electricity.
opportunities.strategic_value_explanation: The EU Innovation Fund is the largest dedicated industrial decarbonisation funding instrument in Europe; success would provide transformational capital for Kelvara's first commercial-scale deployment and establish EU market credibility.
opportunities.ease_explanation: Auction mechanism requires detailed project financials, carbon abatement cost modelling, and a bankable deployment project — highly demanding for a seed-stage company without a completed commercial pilot.
opportunities.opens_date: Next round expected 2026–2027 (first round opened Feb 2025, closed Dec 2025)
opportunities.deadline: Next round deadline unknown — monitor CINEA website
opportunities.project_size_duration: Large-scale deployment projects; typically €5M–€50M+ per project; multi-year
opportunities.consortium_rules: Solo or consortium; EU-registered project entity required as applicant
opportunities.past_similar_projects: First IF25 Heat Auction awarded ~€400M to 65 projects across EU industrial sectors including ceramics, chemicals, and food processing — directly analogous to Kelvara's target customers.
opportunities.notes: Kelvara will need an EU-registered entity or a consortium with an EU industrial partner to apply as lead. The auction mechanism rewards lowest carbon abatement cost — Kelvara's aluminium PCM technology must demonstrate competitive cost per tonne CO2 avoided.
opportunities.reason_for_inclusion: No other EU funding instrument is more precisely targeted at Kelvara's exact value proposition — replacing fossil-fuel industrial process heat with stored renewable electricity at scale.
opportunities.reason_for_caution: The auction mechanism and large project scale requirements may be premature for a seed-stage company at TRL 6 without a completed commercial pilot; Kelvara should target the round following its 5 MWh pilot completion.

company_profile.name: Kelvara Systems
company_profile.value_proposition: Kelvara Systems enables industrial facilities such as food processing, chemicals, and paper plants to replace fossil-fuel process heat with surplus renewable electricity by providing modular, grid-scale thermal batteries that store energy as high-temperature heat in a recycled aluminium-alloy phase-change medium.
company_profile.technology: Modular thermal battery using recycled aluminium-alloy phase-change material (PCM) to store surplus renewable electricity as high-temperature heat; discharge is via direct industrial process heat or electricity generation through an integrated heat engine. Modular architecture supports grid-scale deployment.
company_profile.primary_outcome: Industrial emissions reduction by displacing gas-fired process heat with stored renewable energy, alongside energy cost savings for industrial operators.
secondary_benefits: Grid flexibility through long-duration energy storage absorbing surplus wind and solar
Circular economy benefit via use of recycled aluminium as the storage medium
Dual-output capability — process heat and electricity — increasing asset utilisation
Reduced industrial energy bills through time-shifting cheap renewable electricity
company_profile.trl: TRL 6 — a 500 kWh demonstration unit is operating continuously at a partner site, confirming prototype validation in a relevant industrial environment; first commercial pilot (5 MWh) is in preparation.
company_profile.website_summary: Kelvara Systems is a seed-stage climate-hardware company founded in 2023, headquartered in Wellington, New Zealand with an engineering team and pilot site in Manchester, UK. The company builds modular thermal batteries that store surplus renewable electricity as high-temperature heat in recycled aluminium-alloy phase-change material, discharging it as industrial process heat or electricity. Its target customers are energy-intensive industrial sectors — food processing, chemicals, and paper — seeking to decarbonise heat and reduce energy costs.
company_profile.external_findings: No independent press coverage, funding announcements, or third-party profiles for Kelvara Systems were found in external searches; several unrelated entities share similar names (a German website, a health supplement brand, and a Latin American security firm), suggesting the company has a minimal public digital footprint consistent with its early seed stage founded in 2023. All substantive information about the company derives from the user-provided overview. The absence of external corroboration is typical for early-stage deep-tech hardware startups that have not yet completed a public fundraise or issued press releases.

acronym_definitions.definition: Artificial Intelligence — referenced in the context of digital and AI-based demand-side flexibility solutions targeted by the Innovate UK consumer flexibility programme
Clean Industrial Deal — the European Commission policy framework and associated Horizon Europe R&I call targeting decarbonisation of energy-intensive industries
European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency — the EU body managing the Innovation Fund and other climate-related funding programmes
Cluster 5 — the Horizon Europe thematic cluster covering Climate, Energy and Mobility under which industrial thermal storage projects have previously been funded
European Innovation Council — the EU body that provides funding and support to high-potential deep-tech startups and SMEs through instruments such as the EIC Accelerator
European Union — the supranational political and economic union whose institutions manage the funding programmes described
Horizon Europe Clean Industrial Deal call identifier for the 2026 first round of R&I funding for industrial decarbonisation
Innovation Action — a Horizon Europe project type focused on closer-to-market activities such as demonstration and piloting, typically at higher TRL levels
Industrial Energy Transformation Fund — a UK government grant programme supporting energy-intensive industries to reduce energy use and carbon emissions
Innovation Fund 2025 — the European Commission's 2025 round of the Innovation Fund supporting low-carbon technology deployment
Megawatt-hour — a unit of energy equal to one megawatt of power sustained for one hour, used here to describe the scale of a thermal storage pilot
Phase Change Material — a substance that stores and releases thermal energy during the process of melting and solidifying, used here as Kelvara's heat-storage medium
Research and Innovation — the combined research and innovation activities targeted by Horizon Europe funding calls
Research and Innovation Action — a Horizon Europe project type focused on generating new knowledge, typically at lower TRL levels
Small and Medium-sized Enterprise — a business classification used by EU and UK funders to determine eligibility, typically defined by employee count and turnover thresholds
Technology Readiness Level — a scale from 1 to 9 measuring the maturity of a technology, used by funders to define eligibility thresholds
United Kingdom — the country whose organisations may participate in Horizon Europe as an associated country and which hosts Innovate UK funding programmes
UK Research and Innovation — the UK government body that oversees public funding for research and innovation, of which Innovate UK is a constituent council
